extracted_text: The court may exclude relevant evidence if its probative value is substantially outweighed by a danger of one or more of the following: unfair prejudice, confusing the issues, misleading the jury, undue delay, wasting time, or needlessly presenting cumulative evidence.
axiom_summary: Rule 403 frames consideration as a judicial balancing act: the court weighs probative value against prejudicial danger; this weighing is the evidentiary sense of consideration, orthogonal to contract bargain.
proportional_relation_hint: contract-consideration (exchange inducing promise) : evidence-consideration (probative-vs-prejudicial balancing by judicial officer)
